subject: Sort-merge file description entry
notes: The format is `SD file-name-1 [ record-clause ] .` and nothing else, RENDERED from the printed page (PDF p376 / printed folio 346) rather than read off the OCR. Both halves hold: the record-clause is modelled and the file-name-only spelling parses (the positive golden writes `SD SF RECORD CONTAINS 10 CHARACTERS.`), and the residue is now DIAGNOSED. The rule used to end in a generic file-description clause (`IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER|literal)*`), a shared vendor-extension catch-all that made `SD SF WIBBLE WOBBLE.` compile and run in silence at every edition (kb/Work PB829); it now ends in the ONE `unrecognizedClause` error production, refused by name with COBOL1970. The COBOL-85 DATA RECORDS clause of this format is superset-parsed and removal-gated post-bind. A green witness that the legal clause parses would NOT have been evidence on its own — the row also owes the negative, because an open list can parse every legal clause and still accept anything at all.
